name: Tarshish
title: Son of Javan and ancestor of a seafaring people
summary: Tarshish was a son of Javan, grandson of Japheth, and great-grandson of Noah. He is known as an ancestor of a people and a region associated with distant sea voyages and wealth. The name Tarshish later became linked to a famous port city and trading region, often connected with the western Mediterranean, and is best known as the place the prophet Jonah tried to flee to.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the table of nations
keyEvents.description: Tarshish is mentioned as one of the sons of Javan in the genealogy after the flood, showing how the peoples spread across the earth.

keyEvents.title: Repeated in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: Tarshish's genealogy is repeated in 1 Chronicles as part of Japheth's descendants.

keyEvents.title: Solomon's Tarshish Ships
keyEvents.description: King Solomon had a fleet of Tarshish ships that sailed on long trading voyages and brought back gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.

keyEvents.title: Jonah's Flight to Tarshish
keyEvents.description: The prophet Jonah tried to flee from the Lord's call by taking a ship to Tarshish, the farthest known destination in the west, away from Nineveh.

keyEvents.title: Tarshish in Isaiah's Prophecies
keyEvents.description: The prophet Isaiah prophesies about the destruction of the Tarshish ships and the fall of the city, as well as about Tarshish's future role in bringing God's people back.

keyEvents.title: Tarshish in Ezekiel's Lament over Tyre
keyEvents.description: In Ezekiel's prophecy concerning Tyre, Tarshish is described as an important trading partner that traded in silver, iron, tin, and lead.
